steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place bread cubes in a medium bowl and pour melted butter over top. Add zucchini, onion, egg, and garlic salt; mix well.
Transfer the mixture into a 9x13-inch baking dish and top with cheese.
Cover and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Uncover the dish and bake for another 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Zucchini Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy zucchini casserole bakes diced zucchini with seasoned bread cubes and Cheddar for a simple vegetable side with lots of cheesy goodness.

video.description: Chopped bread, onions, zucchini, and garlic salt get mixed all together before going into a baking dish. Spread an even layer in the baking dish and top with shredded cheddar cheese! Simple, easy, and a delicious side to a meal.
video.name: Cheesy Zucchini Casserole I

review.reviewBody: This is the first time I've cooked with zucchini, other than to just saute or grill it. It was great! I consider recipes to be guidelines and always consider the recipe reviews. Here are the changes I made: I used 2 cups of dry plain bread cubes, 2 eggs, Lawry's seasoning salt, 1 t of jarred roasted garlic, 1 cup of mozzarella (in an attempt to make it lighter), a chopped green onion and 3 cups of zucchini. I also baked it in an 8 by 8 dish. We had it as the main part of the meal and loved it, the bread was perfect and not mushy and the zucchini was tender. It had lots of flavor and the extra egg helped hold it together. It surpassed my expectations and I plan to make it again except make a little more so it fills the 8 by 8 dish more. Thank you for a yummy, inexpensive, beautiful to look at and nutritious recipe!

I made this recently and will be making it anytime I have zucchini in the future! I added some chopped green pepper to the casserole. I also used sharp cheddar cheese. I think I will be trying it with sausage, pepperoni or keilbasa for a main dish.

I have made cheesy zucchini casserole for years, I have found we like it better using saltine crackers crumbs instead of bread and put in a large teaspoon of horseradish sauce, but it was very good without the changes. Thank you for shaing

Like the other adjustments below I added toasted bread and another egg because I had 3 big zucchini’s. I also added minced garlic and thyme and basil for seasonings to the eggs. To make it a full meal I sautéed some cubed chicken breasts and put it on the top pushing it into the zucchini bread mix before the cheese and baked this covered for 30 minutes then when I took off the foil I topped it with cheese. It came out wonderfully !

Good side dish, easy to prepare early in the day & cook later. Can be a complete meal just add some protein. I read other reviews & toasted bread 1st, used mixture of cheese that I had & mixed in, not on top, only 1/2 onion, added salt/pepper & garlic powder. will make this again as it is easy to change up.

I toasted the bread first, I used 2 eggs (could have even used 3 to hold it all together), I mixed some of the cheese into the zucchini mixture, I added a teaspoon or so of dried Italian seasoning (and wished I had added 2), and after putting it all together in the pan, I put the rest of the cheese on top. Then I took a small tomato, scooped out the seeds and jelly, and made thin strips to lay on top. Sprinkled with dried parsley. It came out perfectly and looked so pretty!

I tried this version. I have made many squash casseroles (yellow and zucchini), but I cut a little larger chunks (maybe an inch) that the photos showed. I pre-cook the larger chunks squash (yellow or green) with chopped onion (again, mine are larger than photo), and some water or chicken broth. If using water, I use Better Than Bouillon, Salt, Pepper and some (a lot of) butter. Just enough to soften veggies. I mix in a big bowl, add garlic, S&P to taste. Add more melted butter. If you don't have old/stale/dried bread, use stuffing mix. Doesn't matter what kind. Would need to add a bit more liquid. I use a can of cream of chicken soup. Mix cheese in and also use on top. If using Yellow squash I use Cheddar, if using Zucchini, I substitute part of the cheese with Parmesan. One time I made with neighbors over-abundance of eggplant. Turned out great.

I make this every season as my zucchini plants produce huge quantities and I get creative depending on what I have on hand. I used seasoned stuffing mix instead of bread for a more crunchy texture. I used 2 eggs. I lightly sautéed the onions as I melted the butter. For color I added red peppers and pimentos. For protein I added ham chunks which makes it a main course. I mixed part of the shredded cheese into the dish & added the rest on top when I uncovered it. Don't be shy, this dish needs a lot of cheese to keep it moist. I also added parmesan (cuz I love it) and French fried onion rings (really yummy) on top in the last 20 minutes.

My whole family loved this. We all give it a 5 star rating. I followed recommendations from other reviews. ie. I doubled the recipe. I lightly toasted the bread. I melted the butter and sautéed the onions and zucchini in the butter. I added half of the cheese to the mixture [and sprinkled the other half on top] and I added cubed, cooked chicken. It was delicious.

So easy So good! I used sour dough bread lightly toasted and buttered the slices before cubing. I also used about half of the called for onion, used the grated cheese I had on hand (1 cup mozzarella mixed in and 1 cup grated Mexican on top) We like spicy so I substituted the garlic salt for Cajun seasoning. Used and 8 inch square pan.

This is a great starter that can be easily built into a main dish. I added a pound of hamburger while I sautéed the onion and garlic. I used a box of herb flavored Stop Top instead of bread and added a can of garlic and olive oil flavored diced tomatoes. Delicious!
Made it loved it
I have been making this almost weekly all summer…. My husband and I both love it!
Didn’t make changes

Followed the directions with a few additions. I did use sliced instead of cubed. Added extra butter. Took a lot of suggestions from people’s comments. Toasted the bread, added red pepper, added pimento and extra cheese. Also used mince garlic. My wife loved it. Put in 8x8 pan. Will make this many times.

My grandma use to make a dish almost identical just a bit more of everything and probably a bit more unhealthy lol and it was always one of my favorites. We do pretty much the exact same but we use whatever old bread we have in the pantry, hot dog buns hamburger buns whatever cube it and slightly sauté half an onion, 3 zucchini’s, minced garlic, seasoning salt, and pepper in a whole stick of butter then dump that on the bread let it cool down and then mix it with 10-12 eggs put it in a casserole dish then top it with whatever cheese we have in the fridge and cook at 350 for 30 minutes. My grandma started it then my mom and aunt kept it going now I make it for my family and take to the in laws for holidays and it’s always a crowd pleaser!
I used 4 eggs...I just don't see how 1 egg would have been enough. Maybe some cilantro in it would be tasty or dill.

Zucchinis are coming into the garden like gang busters, and I had to find something to use them up. I started with the recipe, but it looked a little boring, so I added a can of cream of chicken soup, a teaspoon of Lowrey's seasoned salt and Old Bay seasoning. I also added half of the cheese to the mix before putting it into the casserole and sprinkled the rest of the cheese on top. The cheese looked a little skimpy, so I added another half cup before baking it. Oh yeah! What started out as a good basic recipe is now in my rotation as long as the zucchinis keep growing.

We made it but definitely needs something to add flavor to it. I tried hot sauce and that helped a little. Still needs something. But overall, seems like it is a good use of some of the zucchini that are coming in the garden.

Excellent recipe! The only changes I made were adding extra bread, and I did a clove of garlic with Lawrys season salt instead of the garlic salt. Turned out wonderfully, definitely saving to make again in the future.
